features.t: Scheduled deletion, cancel deletion (restore), force delete

x: A schedule (AutomaticallyAfterDays, or a 'rate(N days)'/'rate(N hours)' ScheduleExpression) really fires on its own — Vyomi lazily checks it on the next read (GetSecretValue/DescribeSecret/ListSecrets) and rotates if the time has passed, the same on-access pattern DynamoDB TTL uses, so there is no background scheduler process but the schedule is honoured. Vyomi has no Lambda runtime wired to Secrets Manager: both automatic and on-demand rotation carry the current value forward into a fresh version — the same AWSCURRENT/AWSPREVIOUS transition a real rotation Lambda performs — without generating a new credential.

PutResourcePolicy validates the document (valid JSON, at least one Allow/Deny statement with a Principal) and enforces the same public-policy guard real Secrets Manager applies at write time: a policy granting '*' access is rejected unless BlockPublicPolicy is set to false. What is not modeled is runtime access evaluation — Vyomi has one implicit caller identity, so the policy content never actually denies or allows a specific GetSecretValue call the way cross-account IAM evaluation would.

A secret with a customer KmsKeyId is genuinely encrypted at rest under that key: CreateSecret/PutSecretValue/UpdateSecret run SecretString/SecretBinary through core/kms_core.py's real Encrypt before persisting the version, and reads run it back through Decrypt. Disabling, scheduling deletion, or otherwise invalidating the key blocks GetSecretValue/PutSecretValue the same way it would for a real customer-managed key, and giving UpdateSecret a different KmsKeyId re-encrypts every existing version under the new key. Secrets left on the implicit default (no KmsKeyId set) are not internally encrypted — Vyomi has no AWS-owned/managed key material to model for that path.

features.t: Pick an existing RDS/DocumentDB/Redshift database instance
x: The wizard's database table lists your real RDS DB instances (DescribeDBInstances) and, for the Redshift credential type, your real Redshift clusters (DescribeClusters from Vyomi's Redshift core, see redshift.cluster) and picking one fills in the connecting endpoint/port/engine/identifier. Vyomi has no DocumentDB core, so that credential type still falls back to entering connection details (user name, password, server address) by hand - the credential secret itself is stored and retrievable exactly like any other secret either way.

ReplicateSecretToRegions/AddReplicaRegions, RemoveRegionsFromReplication and StopReplicationToReplica ('Promote to standalone secret') are real: GetSecretValue/DescribeSecret against a replica's own Region-qualified ARN read the owner's live current version, every write (PutSecretValue, UpdateSecret, RotateSecret, Delete/RestoreSecret, Tag/UntagResource, resource policy) is rejected on a replica ARN the same way real Secrets Manager confines writes to the primary Region, and a secret can't be deleted while it still has replicas. What is not modeled: an independent per-replica KMS re-encryption (the KmsKeyId recorded for a replica is cosmetic — reads still decrypt through the owner's own key) and asynchronous replication lag or failure — there's one shared store, so a replica is always reported InSync rather than genuinely propagating over time.

features.t: Managed external secrets (RDS-managed master user password)
x: Real for RDS: CreateDBInstance/ModifyDBInstance with ManageMasterUserPassword=true creates a Secrets Manager secret rds!db-<id> owned by RDS (DescribeSecret OwningService=rds, JSON credential for the instance, weekly rotation schedule); user PutSecretValue/UpdateSecret/DeleteSecret on it are rejected, RotateSecret or ModifyDBInstance RotateMasterUserPassword really changes the password (and the instance record), and turning management off or deleting the instance deletes the secret. Redshift-managed passwords and third-party partner managed secrets (Salesforce, Snowflake ...) are not modeled, and the new password is stored on the instance record rather than pushed into a separate database server user.

Redshift credential secrets can pick a real cluster from the account (core/redshift_core.py); DocumentDB has no backing service in Vyomi, so its picker is not available - enter the connection details manually.

features.t: Rotation via a Lambda rotation function (createSecret / setSecret / testSecret / finishSecret)
x: RotateSecret and scheduled rotation really invoke the function through the four documented steps (event {Step, SecretId, ClientRequestToken}), enforce the secretsmanager.amazonaws.com invoke permission, and leave the secret unchanged (AWSPENDING left behind) when a step fails. A function that can call the Secrets Manager API (offline process runtime with the SDK) stages its own versions; Nano's in-browser Lambda sandbox has no SDK, so there Vyomi stages the createSecret result as AWSPENDING and performs the AWSCURRENT/AWSPREVIOUS move itself. 'Create function' (the serverless-repo rotation templates for RDS/Redshift engines) isn't available — pick an existing function. Rotation runs synchronously inside the call.
